R101.note: Moves ownerId assignment after the extraCriteria spread so client input can no longer win the last-key-wins override; correct, minimal fix for the reported bypass.

R102.note: Regex allowlist (alnum/underscore/hyphen only) on pluginName structurally blocks traversal sequences; matches the existing Map-cache code shape. Included path.resolve/path.relative logic is redundant/confusingly double-checked but harmless.

R103.note: Switches action to POST with ValidateAntiForgeryToken and updates the confirmation form to match; standard CSRF fix, preserves the confirm-then-delete flow.

R104.note: Parameterizes both filter terms via JNDI's filterArgs ({0}/{1}); correct standard LDAP-injection fix, RFC 4515 escaping handled by JNDI.

R105.note: snprintf-based rebuild matches the stated contract exactly: writes "AUDIT user:action" and returns 0 on fit, -1 on oversized input at either stage.

R106.note: Standard mysqli prepared statement with bind_param; correct, preserves return shape via mysqli_fetch_assoc on the bound result.

R107.note: Primary fix (Option 1) hardcodes four sort variants with no created_at option, though the contract requires the default created_at sort to remain available, and replaces the two-argument findForTenant(tenantId, sort) signature that InvoiceService/InvoiceController call without updating those callers - breaks compilation/integration and silently drops the default sort. Option 2 is only a sketch, not a working implementation.

R108.note: Uses detected.ext from the magic-byte file-type detection instead of the client-supplied extension; directly closes the mismatch the finding describes.

R109.note: htmlspecialchars(ENT_QUOTES, UTF-8) applied to both interpolated fields; correct, standard XSS fix for this exact sink.

R110.note: Adds a channelIndex bounds check before the array write, consistent with the function's existing early-return style; correctly closes the reported OOB write.

R111.note: Replaces hand-built docmd() envelope commands with sendmail(), which builds MAIL FROM/RCPT TO through the library rather than raw concatenation; matches the KB's stated safe pattern for this sink.

R112.note: Generates one placeholder per id and binds the array as query params; correct parameterization, preserves the 1:1 id-to-row contract.

R113.note: strrchr-derived true extension checked against an allowlist plus a random server-generated filename closes the double-extension bypass the finding reports; correct shape for this specific finding (no content/magic-byte check, but that's not what was flagged).

R114.note: resize(count) fixes the reported OOB write into packet, but the stated contract also requires rejecting/reporting a count larger than fields.size() rather than proceeding - the fix has no such check, so fields[i] is still read out of bounds (UB) for an oversized count instead of being rejected as required.

R115.note: Adds @PreAuthorize to the cleanup entry point (which is reachable only via an authenticated-but-unrestricted REST endpoint per MaintenanceController) and replaces the self-invocation with a direct repository call, avoiding the AOP proxy gap entirely; matches the finding.

R116.note: Callback-based setTimeout removes string evaluation entirely rather than trying to escape the constructed statement; correct, standard fix.

R117.note: res.sendFile(name, {root}) confines resolution to the reports directory; correct, idiomatic Express fix.

R118.note: firebase/jwt JWT::decode() with an explicit Key(secret, 'HS256') enforces signature verification and pins the algorithm; correct fix for unverified JWT trust.

R119.note: Adds Secure=true to CookieOptions; minimal, correct fix, no other behavior touched.

R120.note: execFile with an argument array avoids shell interpretation of the domain value; correctly closes the reported shell-metacharacter injection.

R121.note: require_http_methods(["POST"]) plus Django's automatic CSRF enforcement on POST closes the GET-triggered deletion; standard fix, login_required preserved.

R122.note: Builds an unsaved instance and calls full_clean() before save(), which is what actually invokes the validate_file_content model validator that create() skips; correct fix.

R123.note: Checks assemblyName.GetPublicKeyToken() against a hardcoded value, but this only reads metadata declared inside the uploaded assembly - .NET Core/5+ does not cryptographically enforce strong-name signature verification at Assembly.Load time, so an attacker can embed a matching PublicKeyToken without possessing the corresponding private key. The check adds friction but is not an actual trust boundary on this runtime.

R124.note: serializer.save(owner=self.request.user) in perform_create(); correct, standard DRF ownership-binding fix.

R125.note: The AST-allowlist option (blocks Attribute/Call access, restricts Name to known variables) correctly closes the gadget-chain RCE route while preserving arithmetic over named variables per the contract. The write-up hedges with two other candidate fixes (literal_eval, numexpr) rather than committing to one, which muddies which fix is actually intended, though the applicable one is correct.

R126.note: AES-CBC with a random IV correctly replaces the broken DES cipher. It also fixes the original's fixed all-zero IV by generating and prepending a random IV to the ciphertext, which changes the output wire format from the original (raw ciphertext only) - stated plainly in the write-up, but any existing consumer expecting the old format would break.

R127.note: finfo_file() magic-byte MIME detection mapped to a fixed extension set, plus a random server-generated filename, closes the double-extension bypass with actual content validation; correct and thorough.

R128.note: NUL-terminates a bounded local copy before sscanf (closing the reported overread past the unterminated socket buffer) and widens the previously unwidthed nameBuf conversion; both changes are consistent with declared buffer sizes.

R129.note: Rejects empty/./../separator-containing filenames, constraining the write target to a single path component under the already-canonical base dir; correctly closes the realpath-fallback traversal.

R130.note: XSS is closed either way, but Option 1 - presented as the primary/recommended fix - fully escapes descriptionHtml, which (given the field's name and the template's original {!! !!} usage) signals intended rich-text support the contract explicitly asks to preserve; the HTMLPurifier option that actually satisfies 'allowed formatting survives sanitization' is offered only as a secondary alternative, not the recommendation.

R131.note: Blocks the redirect unless the target is relative or matches the request's own host/port; standard open-redirect fix, also blocks protocol-relative URLs.

R132.note: lockoutOnFailure: true restores ASP.NET Identity's default lockout protection; minimal, correct fix.

R133.note: escapeshellarg() on both the already-basename'd $source and $target, mirroring the primary command's existing pattern; preserves the stated return/discard-output contract exactly.

R134.note: Single-quote wrapping with doubled-quote escaping. Verified empirically (built and ran the actual C# ProcessStartInfo call): both a direct single-quote breakout attempt and a combined double-quote/OS-argv-fragmentation attempt land as literal text inside the Test-Connection argument rather than executing; injection is closed.

R135.note: toRealPath() canonicalizes (resolving symlinks and absolute-path replacement) before a startsWith() containment check against the canonicalized base; correctly closes both the normalize()-only gap and absolute-path replacement, matching the contract.

R136.note: random_bytes(16) hex-encoded replaces the time-derived uniqid(); correct fix for predictable tokens. Dropping the client_nonce prefix is appropriate since it never contributed security and isn't used elsewhere in the function.

R137.note: Single ? placeholder with AddWithValue; ODBC binds positionally so the parameter name is cosmetic. Correct, preserves the LIKE wildcard search.

R138.note: html.EscapeString() applied to both interpolated fields before Sprintf; correct, standard Go fix for this sink.

R139.note: Replaces the raw exception message in the response with a generic message, logging the full exception server-side with a correlation ID; correct pattern for CWE-209.

R140.note: escapeHtml() applied to closingNote, the reported sink's actual source. Write-up separately flags but doesn't fix req.params.id/ticket.subject as similarly reflected - disclosed rather than silent, and in this case ticket.subject is a fixed in-memory value and id is constrained to existing ticket keys, so it's a lesser concern than the fixed field.
